core_obligations: Reduce to a cohomology-sheaf statement (proof lines 6357-6358): f^*Rf_*K -> K is an isomorphism if and only if it induces isomorphisms on all cohomology sheaves H^j.
Use flatness to commute pullback with cohomology (proof lines 6359-6360): H^j(f^*Rf_*K) = f^*H^j(Rf_*K) = f^*H^j(Rf_* tau_{<= j}K) = H^j(f^*Rf_* tau_{<= j}K), so one may assume K is bounded.

Place K in the subcategory D' (proof lines 6361-6364): hypothesis (3) says the cohomology sheaves lie in D', and since D' is a triangulated subcategory and K is bounded, K itself lies in D', which is the assertion that f^*Rf_*K -> K is an isomorphism.
proof_roadmap: Check the map on cohomology sheaves instead of on the objects.
Flatness of f makes pullback commute with cohomology sheaves, and truncation makes the relevant piece bounded, so K may be assumed bounded.
By hypothesis each cohomology sheaf lies in the subcategory D' of the earlier lemma.
Boundedness and stability of D' under distinguished triangles put K itself in D'.
difficulty_reason: The lemma gives a criterion for the unit f^*Rf_*K -> K to be an isomorphism for a flat morphism of ringed topoi and a bounded below K (statement lines 6343-6354). The proof is a reduction: one passes to cohomology sheaves, uses flatness of f so that pullback commutes with taking cohomology sheaves, H^j(f^*Rf_*K) = f^*H^j(Rf_*K), and the truncation identity H^j(Rf_*K) = H^j(Rf_* tau_{<= j}K) to reduce to a bounded K, after which hypothesis (3) puts each cohomology sheaf in the subcategory D' of the earlier upstairs lemma and boundedness plus stability under triangles puts K there (proof lines 6357-6364). The non-formal content is the combination of the truncation reduction with flatness; the claim is H2.
